deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. The page determines the latitude (Polhöhe) of Göttingen, presumably at the old observatory. It uses zenith distances of Polaris (α Ursae minoris) at lower culmination, measured with a repeating circle on 20 March–8 April 1813. The previous and next pages hold the raw series: multiples of the zenith distance divided by n, a reduction to the meridian, refraction of about 49–51", and the formula φ = 180° − z − δ. For example, 26 March: 180° − 40°9'24.71" − 88°18'37.92" = 51°31'57.37". The present page (1) computes the apparent place of Polaris for each observing night and (2) combines the nightly latitudes into a weighted mean.

(1) APPARENT PLACE. The mean place is α0 = 0h55m14.27s (annual variation 13.750 s) and δ0 = 88°18'37.665" (annual variation 19.408").

For each date t (fraction of year τ, about 0.2164 on 20 March and 0.2685 on 8 April) the right ascension, in seconds of time, is
- α = α0 + 13.750·τ + A_α + N_α.
- A_α (aberration) = 10^1.62596 · sin(☉ + 254°59'11") = 42.27 s · sin(☉ + 255.0°). The 'Constanten' are logarithms of the amplitudes.
- N_α (nutation) = 10^1.33778 · sin(Ω + 256°46') = 21.77 s · sin(Ω + 256.8°).
- Rows: precession +2.976 … +3.692; aberration −40.817 … −42.175; nutation +12.250 … +11.992.
- Sums: −25.59, −25.90, −26.38, −26.69, −26.73, −26.61, −26.49.
- Apparent RA: 0h54m48.68s, 48.38, 47.91, 47.61, 47.54, 47.66, 47.78.

The declination is
- δ = δ0 + 19.408·τ + A_δ + N_δ.
- A_δ = 10^1.30323 · sin(☉ + 167°57') = 20.10" · sin(☉ + 167.95°).
- N_δ = 10^0.86605 · sin(Ω + 161°43') = 7.346" · sin(Ω + 161.7°).
- Rows: precession +4.211 … +5.201; aberration +4.202 … −2.334, changing sign near ☉ ≈ 12°, i.e. 2 April; nutation −6.413 … −6.463.
- Sums: +2.000, +1.413, +0.240, −1.243, −2.128, −3.307, −3.586.
- Apparent δ = 88°18' + 39.66", 39.08, 37.90, 36.42, 35.54, 34.36, 34.08.

These amplitudes and phases are the star-specific sinusoidal forms of the classical formulas, my derivation:
- Aberration in RA: Δα cosδ = −κ(cosα cosε cos☉ + sinα sin☉).
- Aberration in Dec: Δδ ≈ −κ(cosα sinδ sin☉ − sinα sinδ cosε cos☉ + …).
- With α = 13.8°, ε = 23.47°, κ ≈ 20.2" these give phases 255.0° and about 167.3–168° and amplitudes 42.3 s and 20.1".
- Nutation, with Δψ ≈ −A sinΩ and Δε ≈ B cosΩ (A ≈ 17.6", B ≈ 9.6"), gives phases of about 257° and 161.4° and amplitudes of about 21.8 s and 7.2".
- The page's values imply Ω ≈ 137.5°, consistent with the lunar node in early 1813 (about 138°).

Culmination clock times: 12h + apparent α, plus a clock term near +6m50s (50.4, 51.6, 49.9, 51.9, 49.64, 49.25, 49.38), plus a chronometer correction.
- The chronometer correction runs −0m38.0s, −1m33.00s, −3m26.5s, −5m57.6s, −7m46.00s, then −32.25s and −42.30s. It grows about 30 s/day and was evidently reset between 3 and 7 April.
- The −3m26.5s matches 'Kampe zurück 3'26"' on the previous page, i.e. Kampe's chronometer.
- Results: 13h1m1s, 13h0m7s, 12h58m11s, 12h55m42s, 12h53m51s, 13h1m5s, 13h0m55s. Example, 22 March: 12h54m48.38s + 6m51.6s − 1m33.00s = 13h0m6.98s.
- These are the instants about which the meridian reductions on the neighbouring pages are symmetric; the reduction is 0.00 at 12h58m0s on 26 March and at 12h55m40s on 31 March.

(2) RESULTS FOR THE LATITUDE. For each series i with n_i observations, φ_i = 51°31'54" + x_i. Gauss tabulates n_i·x_i, the cumulative Σn_i x_i and Σn_i, and the running weighted mean 54" + Σn x / Σn.

| Date | n | φ_i | n·x | Σn | Σn·x | running mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 Mar | 10 | 54.86 | 8.60 | 10 | 8.60 | 54.86 |
| 22 Mar | 18 | 55.73 | 31.14 | 28 | 39.74 | 55.42 |
| 26 Mar | 18 | 57.40 | 61.20 | 46 | 100.94 | 56.19 |
| 31 Mar | 18 | 56.25 | 40.50 | 64 | 141.44 | 56.21 |
| 3 Apr | 18 | 56.55 | 45.90 | 82 | 187.34 | 56.28 |
| 7 Apr | 20 | 55.35 | 27.0 | 102 | 214.34 | 56.10 |
| 7 Apr | 12 | 54.90 | 10.80 | 114 | 225.14 | 55.97 |
| 8 Apr | 22 | 57.34 | 73.48 | 136 | 298.62 | 56.19 |

Final weighted latitude: 51°31'56.2". Two separate series were reduced on 7 April. The 26 March value 57.40 equals the previous page's 57.37 corrected for the revised declination (37.90 instead of 37.92). The 3 April value 56.55 agrees with the next page (z = 40°9'27.91", δ = 88°18'35.54").
errors: 8 April, declination sum: +5.201 − 2.334 − 6.463 = −3.596, not −3.586 as written. The apparent declination should therefore be 34.07", not 34.08" (a slip of 0.01").

Declination precession entries are slightly inconsistent with the RA precession entries, which imply a common τ. On 20 March τ = 2.976/13.75 = 0.21644 gives 4.201, but 4.211 is written. On 22 March 4.306 is expected, 4.315 written. On 8 April 5.21 is expected, 5.201 written. Effects are at most about 0.01" and negligible.

Apparent RA on 26 and 31 March: 14.27 − 26.38 = 47.89 (47.91 written) and 14.27 − 26.69 = 47.58 (47.61 written). The other dates agree exactly. These are differences of 0.02–0.03 s, immaterial for the latitude because RA is used only to time the culmination.

31 March latitude: the previous page gave 56.27" with δ = 36.45". Recomputing with the revised δ = 36.42" would give 56.30", but 56.25" is entered, overwritten. The weighted column and cumulative sum (100.94 + 40.50 = 141.44) use 56.25.

7 April (20 observations): the column shows 26.0 (or is so transcribed). However, (55.35 − 54) × 20 = 27.0, and the later cumulative 225.14 = 214.34 + 10.80 requires 27.0. So 26.0 is either a slip or a misreading, and the cumulative is 214.34, not 213.34.
Final mean: 298.62/136 = 2.1957, giving 51°31'56.196", which rounds to 56.20". Gauss writes 56.19 (truncation).

results.what: Reduction of Polaris from mean to apparent place by precession, plus aberration and nutation written as star-specific single sinusoids. The aberration amplitudes and phases (log amplitudes 1.62596 and 1.30323; phases 254°59'11" and 167°57') are computed for α ≈ 13.8°, δ ≈ 88.3°.
results.modern_name: Apparent place reduction (precursor of Besselian star constants / day numbers)
results.usually_credited_to: Bradley (aberration 1729, nutation 1748); formulas by Euler, Lagrange, Delambre, Zach; systematized by Bessel (Tabulae Regiomontanae, 1830)

results.what: Clock times of lower culmination: 12h + apparent RA, corrected by the clock and Kampe chronometer offsets.
Latitude from circum-meridian zenith distances of Polaris at lower culmination (φ = 180° − z − δ), combined by a mean weighted by the number of observations: 51°31'56.2".
results.modern_name: Latitude determination with a repeating circle; weighted arithmetic mean

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine observatory reduction work from Gauss's early Göttingen years (1813). Gauss's latitude determinations at Göttingen are well documented. The only mildly interesting feature is the compact star-specific sinusoidal form of aberration and nutation, a precursor of later star constants, but such forms were common practice.

checkable.asserts: Dec correction sum for 8 April = -3.596 (Gauss wrote -3.586)
Aberration in RA for sun longitude 0° is about -40.8 s (written -40.817)
Aberration in Dec for sun longitude 0° is about +4.20" (written +4.202)
Phase of RA aberration for α = 13.8° is about 255°, matching 254°59'
RA aberration amplitude is about 42.3 s, matching 10**1.62596
Dec precession implied by the RA fraction on 20 March is about 4.201 (Gauss wrote 4.211)
Weighted mean latitude seconds = 56.196, i.e. φ = 51°31'56.20"
Lower-culmination formula φ = 180° - z - δ gives 57.37" for 26 March (previous page)
Clock time of culmination on 22 March = 13h0m6.98s (written 13 0 7)

transcription_corrections: '−0,38,0', '−1,33,00', etc. are clock corrections in minutes and seconds: −0m38.0s, −1m33.00s, −3m26.5s, −5m57.6s, −7m46.00s, −0m32.25s, −0m42.30s.
In the weighted-sum column for 31 March, '40,80' is probably 40,50: the cumulative 100.94 + 40.50 = 141.44 and the value 56.25 require it.
In the 7 April (n = 20) row, the cumulative is likely 214,34, not 213,34, since 214.34 + 10.80 = 225.14 as written next. The entry '26,0' is either 27,0 or a slip by Gauss.
The 'Constanten' 1,62596, 1,30323, 1,33778, 0,86605 are base-10 logarithms of the amplitudes (42.27 s, 20.10", 21.77 s, 7.346"), not the amplitudes themselves.

The heading reads 'Berechnung der Positionen von α Ursae' (Polaris, α Ursae minoris). The bracketed note at the foot is in a different, apparently later hand. 'am Ubos 8.4.1813' is uncertain; only the date 8.4.1813 is secure.
